summary: Today’s pulse tracks Trump focuses on Washington DC construction projects on eve of midterm election as Democrats climb in polls – live, Third person dies of bird flu since virus started jumping to livestock, and Russian bombing kills 26 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says. Across Guardian, Ars Technica, and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are stevens, campaign, and rogers. In the background, ‘A despicable betrayal’: Democrats incensed by Haley Stevens’s endorsement of Mike Rogers and Ex-FBI chief in Chicago sues DoJ, claiming he was pressured to investigate Trump’s foes keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Trump focuses on Washington DC construction projects on eve of midterm election as Democrats climb in polls – live
headlines.description: President at reflecting pool in Washington DC to talk about various projects in final appearance before Americans head to polls to vote in crucial midterm election The survey took place before Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens announced that she would back Rogers in the contest – a vital seat for her party to retain in their quest for control of the Senate.

headlines.description: The threat is still considered to be low, but the virus continues to spread.

headlines.title: Russian bombing kills 26 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
headlines.description: Officials say at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit a southern Ukrainian village in what the president called an "utterly horrific" attack.

headlines.title: ‘A despicable betrayal’: Democrats incensed by Haley Stevens’s endorsement of Mike Rogers
headlines.description: Stevens’s decision sparked fierce backlash from members of the party, while Donald Trump praised the sudden switch Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens’ shocking last-minute endorsement of Mike Rogers, a Republican Senate candidate, in the run-up to the elections has sparked fierce backlash from members of her party. Stevens, who narrowly lost in the Democratic primary for Senate to Abdul El-Sayed, announced her support for Rogers after a feud with the El-Sayed campaign over an outside group’s campaign ad that blamed the high cost of living on US support for Israel.

headlines.title: Ex-FBI chief in Chicago sues DoJ, claiming he was pressured to investigate Trump’s foes
headlines.description: Douglas DePodesta says he was made ‘scapegoat’ after collapse of case against Broadview Six anti-ICE protesters The former head of the FBI in Chicago has accused the Trump administration of pressuring him to investigate the president’s political opponents and making him a “scapegoat” after a major federal case against anti-ICE protesters fell apart. Douglas DePodesta, who served as FBI special agent in charge from 2024 until July 2026, alleged in a federal lawsuit filed on Monday that the Department of Justice (DoJ) had engaged in “misconduct” and “malfeasance” in its pursuit of unjust prosecutions – and that he was wrongly blamed for the DoJ’s missteps and unlawfully forced out of his job.

headlines.title: US midterms campaign 'shattering' spending records to be most expensive ever
headlines.description: The 2026 campaign is projected to cost nearly $12bn - BBC Verify looks into where all that money has come from.

headlinePool.title: Trump unveils results of $14m reflecting pool makeover in final appeal before midterms
headlinePool.description: US president shares delayed results of chaotic renovation on DC site as Americans prepare to head to the polls Donald Trump unveiled the delayed results of his $14m renovation of Washington DC’s Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool in what is expected to be his final press conference before voters head to the polls for the midterm elections. On the eve of a consequential election day, with polls indicating that most voters feel the US president has grown too focused on building projects in the nation’s capital, he stood in front of the newly opened reflecting pool to discuss – in detail – changes to the pool’s pipe, the grass surrounding the area and granite.

headlinePool.title: Migration is a moral issue for Burnham – but he also wants to tell a positive story
headlinePool.description: While PM is keen to support those making a contribution his backing of Shabana Mahmood’s hard line is no surprise How will UK immigration rules change under Shabana Mahmood’s latest plans? While out on the campaign trail in Makerfield, Andy Burnham gave a glimpse into where he might land on Labour’s plans for immigration reform, which had already been decried by the left of the party as unfair and pushed by the right as electorally necessary. Asked what he thought of Reform’s attack on “open borders Andy” – Nigel Farage’s early attempt to define him as soft on migration – the then Manchester mayor dismissed the charge as “ridiculous” and went on the defensive.

headlinePool.title: Man guilty of stealing cash from farm owned by South African president
headlinePool.description: The case, part of the "Farmgate" scandal, has left President Cyril Ramaphosa mired in an impeachment saga.

headlinePool.title: AI chatbots are becoming political advisers. Their answers can mislead voters
headlinePool.description: Millions of Americans are turning to AI for election information, but chatbots are getting voting facts wrong and recommending candidates, raising concerns they could influence voters' decisions.

headlinePool.title: Fossilised red blood cells found in 115m-year-old dinosaur’s bone, say scientists
headlinePool.description: Chemical tests on Aratasaurus bone identify presence of heme, the organic compound that allows haemoglobin in blood to carry oxygen around body It could be the opening of a Jurassic Park rip-off: scientists examining ancient dinosaur bones find what appear to be fossilised red blood cells, and traces of the molecule that gives the beast’s blood its distinctive crimson hue. But that is what researchers are claiming to have discovered after analysing the hind leg bones of a small, meat-eating dinosaur called an Aratasaurus that lived and died in what is now north-eastern Brazil 115m years ago.

headlinePool.title: Is America really that polarized? The answer might be a surprise
headlinePool.description: The U.S. has become more politically polarized, but research shows people overestimate their differences and there is 'messy middle' majority of Americans who share overlapping political views.

headlinePool.title: ‘We cannot move forward’: Savannah Guthrie shares new post seeking information in mother’s disappearance
headlinePool.description: Her latest plea comes three months after urging ‘someone to come forward’ with details about Nancy Guthrie Savannah Guthrie has issued a new plea for help on the whereabouts of her 84-year-old mother, who authorities believe was abducted in February. On Sunday, the Today show co-host shared a photo of an old drawing made by her daughter featuring an umbrella and the words: “I know it might not seem like it but I really need my mommy.”

headlinePool.title: Copilot in deadly Florida jet crash identified in reports as 20-year-old
headlinePool.description: In air traffic audio, a crew member can be heard shouting: "We are going to crash into the ground!"

headlinePool.title: Russell Brand is not a ‘psychopath who rapes people and thinks it’s normal’, court told
headlinePool.description: Defence barrister says earlier allegations about comedian’s sexual conduct ‘poisoned the wells’ of justice as trial continues Russell Brand is not a “psychopath who rapes people and thinks it’s normal” and is respectful when women say no, a court has heard. In his closing speech at Southwark crown court, Brand’s barrister, Ian Winter KC, questioned why Brand’s accusers had not fought back when they were allegedly raped, saying “not one of them resisted or screamed or even tried to leave”.
